questions.question: ‘Ankiya Nats’ are one-act plays distinct to the culture of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ‘**Ankiya Nats**’ are one-act plays distinct to the culture of **Assam.**__
 
• Ankia Naats are a class of one act plays performed in** Assam, India.**
 
• The invention of the Ankia Naat is usually attributed to the medieval saint and social reformer **Srimanta Sankardeva.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a89cfbbafd2d9c8bd9e365fa0d722bb05b3e19f8d40277d3469fc8a5044b5577.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Assam is the meeting ground of** diverse cultures.**
 
• The people of the enchanting state of Assam are an intermixture of various racial stocks such as **Mongoloid, Indo-Burmese, Indo-Iranian and Aryan.**
 
• Assam is known for **Assam tea and Assam silk.**
 
• The state was the first site for **oil drilling in Asia.**
 
• Assam is home to the **one-horned Indian rhinoceros, along with the wild water buffalo, pygmy hog, tiger and various species of Asiatic birds,** and provides one of the last wild habitats for the **Asian elephant.**

questions.question: The famous musician, Appa Jalgaonkar is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harmonium.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **​Appa Jalgaonkar** played the **harmonium.**
 
• He was well-known as accompanist of **singer Bhimsen Joshi.**
 
• **Amir Khan, Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, and Hirabai Barodekar** were some of the **singers** with whom Appa Jalgaonkar collaborated.
 
• He was given the **prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Award **for his accomplishments in harmonium playing.
 
• On **September 16th,** he passed away in **Pune at the age of 87.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Harmonium:**

 
 
• It is a **free-reed keyboard** instrument.
 
• It emits sound when air is forced through **metal reeds screwed over slots** in metal frames with close tolerance by** foot-operated bellows** through a **pressure-equalizing air reservoir.**
 
 
 
• **Tabla:**
 
 
• It is the most widely used instrument for **dance, vocal, and instrumental music.**
 
 
 
• **Sarod**:
 
 
• It is a stringed musical instrument of the lute family that is common to the **Hindustani music.**
 
 
 
• **Violin:**
 
 
• It is a **wooden chordophone,** a **type of string instrument.**

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated during the spring season in Jharkhand when sal trees wear new leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Sarhul**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sarhul festival, the most popular tribal celebration across the Jharkhand region, was celebrated on 4 April 2022.
 
• Sarhul means **worshipping trees**. It is celebrated during the spring season when the saal trees wear new leaves
 
• It is celebrated by the tribal communities of the local Sarna religion, most notably by the Munda, Ho, and Oraon tribes.
 
• It is celebrated at the beginning of spring every year in the first month of the Hindu calendar, on the third day of the moon or the fortnight of **‘Chaitra’**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The unmarried tribal girls celebrate the Jawa festival, which has its own kind of song and dance.

 
 
• This is held mainly for the expectation of good fertility and a better household.
 
 
 
• Sohrai is a harvest festival of the Indian states of Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
 
• It is also called the cattle festival.
 
 
 
• Karam is a harvest festival celebrated in the Indian states of Jharkhand, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam, Odisha and West Bengal.

questions.question: Which folk dance represents a mock fight between Goddess Durga and Mahishasura?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dandiya Raas.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raas or Dandiya rass** is a** socio-religious folk danc**e, that originated in the **Gujarat region of India.**
 
• It is frequently done during the **Navaratri celebration.**
 
• The dance is done in **Rajasthan's Marwar.**
 
• Sanskrit terms **"Nava" (which means "Nine") and "Ratri" (which means nights) **are used to celebrate the **Hindu deity Shakti,** which means **Strength or Power.**
 
• With the help of Dandiya Raas, the** nine manifestations **of Shakti/Devi are worshipped.
 
• This traditional dance depicts a f**ictitious conflict between Mahishasura and Goddess Durga.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhangra:**

 
 
• Bhangra is a traditional **folk dance of Punjab.**
 
• It takes place during the **harvesting season.**
 
• Bhangra is particularly connected to the** springtime Vaisakhi festival.**
 
 
 
• **Raslila:**
 
 
• The Raslila or Ras dance is a scene from the **popular Krishna tale** found in Hindu scriptures, in which** Krishna dances with Radha and Braj gopis.**
 
 
 
• **Kalbelia:**
 
 
• The Kalbelia are a snake-taming tribe from Rajasthan, India's Thar Desert.
 
• Men play the instruments and give the music, but only women perform it.

questions.question: Which is one of the most famous dance forms of Assam performed by the 'Kulis' (people who work in the tea gardens) during autumn?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Jhumur dance.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jhumur is a traditional dance of the tea ethnical communities of Assam **and also in some corridors of **West Bengal.**
 
• It's generally performed in the crop season and carnivals.
 
• The main players of the **act are girls, but the music, lyrics, and instruments for the performance are maintained by the manly players.**
 
• Jhumur dance is substantially performed on carnivals like Karam puja and Tushu puja.
 
• Karam puja is one of the most important carnivals for the tea lines.
 
• It's a week-long festivity to worship Karam Raja.
 
• For an entire week, songs are sung, balls are danced, and people stay up late at night to celebrate and worship.

 [IMAGE: https://3.bp.blogspot.com/-zydoF8tG690/V-PBGP85G-I/AAAAAAAABuM/a4umezoU5FoigveGdL-IHosI1h08tSXHACLcB/s1600/2222.jpg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahasu Dance:**

 
 
• Mahasu is one of the colourful forms of the Nati folk dance of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The dance is called Mahasu presumably because it began in the region of the Mahasu Pahari-speaking area.
 
• In Himachal Pradesh, Mahasu Pahari is spoken in a veritably large region which includes further than ten lakh people.
 
• It's substantially spoken in Shimla and Solan.
 
 
 
• **Lambadi dance:**
 
 
• Lambadi dance is a folk dance of the Banjara tribe.
 
• It originated in the Anupu Village of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• A lot of folk dances have originated in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. 
 
 
 
• **Karga dance:**
 
 
• Karaga folk dance is a traditional dance devoted to Draupadi.
 
• It is performed on a full moon night. It is also known as Droupthamma.
 
• Karaga is celebrated by the Tigala group in the Karnataka region.

questions.question: Mahavir Jayanti is a major festival of the ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahavir Jayanti is celebrated by the Jain community commemorating the birth of Lord Mahavira, the founder of Jainism. 
 
• Mahavira is the 24th and the last Tirthankara, who preached the essence of life, virtue, and non-violence towards all living beings.
 
• According to the Swetambaras, he was born in 599 BC but the Digambar school of Jainism believes that Mahavira was born in 615 BC. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Lord Mahavir, also referred to as Indian sage Vardhamana, was born in Kundalagrama, Bihar, as a son to king Siddartha and Queen Trishala. 
 
• At the age of 30, he renounced his throne and other worldly possessions and spent twelve years of his life as an ascetic.
 
• At the age of 72, he attained nirvana and devoted the rest of his life to preach spiritual freedom.

questions.question: Who among the following became the Director General of Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in 1861 and is often called the ‘Father of Indian Archaeology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alexander Cunningham.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alexander Cunningham became the Director General of Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in 1861 and is often called the ‘Father of Indian Archaeology.**
 
• Alexander noted that the amount of brick taken from the ancient site was enough to lay bricks for about **100 miles of the railway line between Lahore and Multan.**
 
• Alexander Cunningham was a British army engineer who later took an interest in the history and archaeology of India.
 
• The Archaeological Survey of India is an Indian government agency, It was founded in **1861 by Alexander Cunningham.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **James Princep:**

 
 
• He was a European scholar who deciphered the edicts of the Ashoka.
 
• He was an English scholar, orientalist, and antiquarian.
 
• He was the founding editor of the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal.
 
• He is best remembered for his understanding of the Kharosthi and Brahmi scripts of ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Allan Octavian Hume:**
 
 
• He was a retired English ICS officer, who formed the Indian National Union in 1885.
 
• The idea of the Indian National Union took shape and Hume initially had some support from Lord Dufferin for this, although the latter wished to have no official link to it.
 
• In March 1885, when a notice was first issued to convene the first Indian National Union to meet at Poona the following December.
 
• In May 1885, Hume secured the viceroy's approval to create an "Indian National Union", which would be affiliated with the government and act as a platform to voice Indian public opinion.

questions.question: Which of the following is an agricultural festival celebrated by tribals in Madhya Pradesh and some other states of India, in the month of September-October every year in honour of the God of youth and power?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Karama Festival.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karama Festival** is an agricultural festival celebrated by tribals in Madhya Pradesh and some other states of India, in the month of September-October every year in honour of the God of youth and power.

 
• The Karama Festival is widely celebrated and popular among the tribal people of Sundargarh, Mayurbhanj, Sambalpur, Bolangir, Dhenkanal, and Keonjhar.

 
 
• The deity worshipped in the festival is either 'Karam', a God, or 'Karamsani', a Goddess who is represented with a branch of the Karam tree.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Thrissur Pooram** is an annual temple festival held in Thrissur, Kerala, India.

 
 
• It is held at the** Vadakkunnathan (Shiva) Temple in Thrissur.**
 
 
 
• The **Chandanakudam festival** was conducted on the eve of the Pettathullal (ceremonial mass dance) held at the Nainar Masjid (Vavar Palli) at **Erumeli, Kerala.**
 
• **Attukal Pongala is a 10-day **religious festival celebrated at the Attukal Bhagavathy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram in the Indian state of **Kerala**.

questions.question: Ugadi Pachadi is a famous dish that is associated with the Ugadi festival of south India. How many different types of ingredients does it contain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Six**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ugadi Pachadi** is a festive food drink made up of **six different flavours**.
 
• As a result, Ugadi Pachadi has six flavours that correspond to the six emotions of life.
 
• After presenting it to the gods, it is the first dish eaten at the Ugadi festival.
 
• Apart from the health advantages of this festive drink, Ugadi Pachadi also means accepting life in all of its forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **According to the Hindu calendar, Ugadi or Yugadi** is the Hindu New Year's Day, which is observed in the Indian states of **Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.**
 
• On the first day of the Hindu lunisolar calendar month of Chaitra, it is celebrated festively in these areas. 
 
• The Pachadi is a popular festive dish that incorporates a wide range of flavours, including sweet, sour, salty, bitter, astringent, and spicy.
 
• It is a symbolic reminder in Telugu and Kannada Hindu traditions that one should expect a wide range of experiences in the approaching new year and make the most of them.

questions.question: Who among the following Indian classical dancers, who popularised the Odissi dance form both in India and all over the world, received the honour of Padma Vibhushan in 2000?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kelucharan Mohapatra.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kelucharan Mohapatra was a legendary Indian classical dancer and a prominent Odissi dance teacher.
 
• He was born on 8th January 1926 and led this dancing talent toward great heights until his death on April 7, 2004.
 
• He is amazingly the** first-ever winner of the Padma Vibhushana Award from the state of Odisha.**
 
• He also got **Padma Bhushan (1988), Padma Shri (1974****), and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1966).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pankaj Charan Mohapatra:**

 
 
• Aptly appertained to as the ‘adiguru’ of Odissi, Guru Pankaj Charan Das was the practitioner of all the authors- fathers of Odissi cotillion – Kelucharan Mohapatra, Mayadhar Raut, and Debaprasad Das – piecemeal from the utmost of the coming generation of Odissi exponents who are internationally known moment.
 
• And ironically, he'd been the most obscure Odissi legend.
 
 
 
• **Rahul Acharya:**
 
 
• Dancer, choreographer, experimenter, Sanskrit scholar, speaker, and pen, Rahul Acharya was the 2014 philanthropist of the Aditya Vikram Birla Kalakiran Award.
 
• In 2013 he entered the Ram Gopal Award for Best Male Solo Dancer from the Dance History Society of India.
 
• Mr. Acharya came the first manly Odissi cotillion recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi with the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar Award in 2009.
 
 
 
• **Debasis Patnaik:**
 
 
• Debasis Patnaik( born 9 June 1967) is an Indian Politician from Odisha, Advocate, and Social Activist of character, who has served as a Member of the Legislative Assembly from Banki, Odisha, during 2004- 2009.
 
• He was formerly the Deputy Chief Whip of the Congress Legislature Party in Odisha Assembly 5 times during his stint as an MLA.
 
• He at present is serving as the Vice – chairman of the Pradesh Congress Committee, Odisha, and a Member of the All India Congress Committee( AICC).

questions.question: The famous musician Satyadev Pawar is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Violin.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Satya Dev Pawar began his study of music at the age of eleven in the quondam Jodhpur State of Rajasthan, **India.
 
• Late His Highness Maharaja Hanumant Singhji patronized youthful **Pawar to train on the violin under Ustad Ali Akbar Khan( the notorious son of Baba Allauddin Khan) therefore continuing the unbroken musical lineage," the Seni Baba Allaudin Gharana," descended from Mian Tansen,** the principal musician in the Moghul Emperor Akbar's court in 15th century India.
 
• latterly, Satyadev Pawar apprenticed under Pandit Ravi Shankar, another outstanding Baba convert, gained fame as one of the best-known shishyas of these great Gurus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ecadfa2aebbde6f5d8518a1b79e60590ca022b7aa48797ddac8c90a13d89ae3a.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shehnai:**

 
 
• Shehnai is a wind instrument made of **wood **and** metal**.
 
• Used in religious observances, this instrument is set up in the colorful corridor of North India.
 
• It's considered to be an auspicious instrument and is played in social observances.
 
• Also a Northern Indian musical instrument.
 
• Some important shehnai players are** Anant Lal**, **Bismillah Khan**, **S. Ballesh**, **Ali Ahmed Hussain Khan**, and **Raghunath Prasanna**.
 
 
 
• **Veena:**
 
 
• Firstly created in the** south of India**, the veena is a plucked string instrument.
 
• This actually belongs to the family of **chordophone instruments **of India.
 
• The veena in numerous corridors of the country has different types which are **Rudra Veena**, **Sarasvati Veena**, and **Vichitra Veena**.
 
• **Carnatic music**, in the south of India, extensively uses the veena.
 
 
 
• **Sitar:**
 
 
• Sitar is a generally used stringed instrument in South Asian countries similar to **Bangladesh**, **India**, and **Sri Lanka**.
 
• The Sitar instrument is a plucked stringed instrument that contains portable frets and a gourd resonator.
 
• “ Sitar ” is deduced from the Persian word “ Sehtar ”( seh navigator) meaning “**three-stringed**”.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is held on a new moon day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kali Puja.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kali Puja or Shyama Puja is conducted in temples as well as at homes, with people worshipping the Goddess Kali on the new moon day of Krishna Paksha in the Kartik month of the Hindu calendar.**
 
• The** festival, which often falls on the same day as Diwali,** is considered auspicious for worshipping the goddess.
 
• Kali Puja (Kali worship) is** celebrated in states of east India especially Bengal, Odisha, Bihar, and Assam** on the new moon night (Amavasya) of the Hindu month Kartik which normally occurs in the** month of October or November** every year.
 
• **It is one of the biggest festivals in Bengal along with Durga Puja.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahavir Jayanti**

 
 
• ​Mahavir Janma Kalyanak is one of the most important **religious festivals in Jainism.**
 
• It** celebrates the birth of Mahavir, the twenty-fourth and last Tirthankara.**
 
• On the Gregorian calendar,** the holiday occurs either in March or April.**
 
 
 
• **​Dussehra**
 
 
• **​Vijayadashami** is also known** as Dussehra, Dasara, or Dashain.**
 
• It is a major** Hindu festival celebrated at the end of Navaratri every year.**
 
• It marks the end of Ramlila and remembers **God Rama's victory over Ravana.**
 
• Alternatively, **it marks a reverence for one of the aspects of the goddess Devi, such as Durga or Saraswati.**
 
 
 
• **Holi​**
 
 
• ​Holi is a popular ancient Hindu festival, also known as the Festival of Spring, the Festival of Colours, or the Festival of Love.
 
• The festival celebrates the eternal and divine love of Radha Krishna.
 
• Holi is celebrated on the** full moon day** in the month of Phalgun.

questions.question: In which Indian state is the 'Fatorpa Zatra' celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**____**.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Fatorpa Zatra** is one of the most famous zatras of Goa and is celebrated at the temple of **Shantadurga Kuncolienkarin at Fatorpa in Quepem taluka.**
 
• 'Kuncolienkarin' means 'from Cuncolim'.
 
• During the **festival**, people from all over Goa, belonging to different religions, communities and castes come to worship the deity.
 
• The zatra is held for** five days during December or January,** during** paushya shuddha panchami upto dashmi of the Hindu calendar.**
 
• The highlight of this event is the chariot procession over four days.
 
• The first day is called Hathi Ambari, which includes an elephant chariot.
 
• The second day is the procession of the flower chariot, popularly known as Fulancho Rath.
 
• The procession of the Vijayrath, a chariot of horses, is held on the third day.
 
• The Maharath procession, which has the main chariot is held on the last day and is thronged by crowds of devotees, marking the finale of the zatra rituals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Goa is also known for its beaches, ranging from popular stretches at Baga and Palolem to those in laid-back fishing villages such as Agonda.

questions.question: Thiruvathira is a cultural festival of which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The cultural festival Thiruvathira is celebrated in the Indian state of **Kerala**.
 
• It is a unique dance performed by women seeking blessings for marital bliss on **Lord Shiva's** birthday in the month of **Dhanu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi currently confers classical status on eight Indian classical dance styles:-

 
 
• Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu)
 
• Kathak (North, West and Central India)
 
• Kathakali (Kerala)
 
• Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh)
 
• Odissi (Orissa)
 
• Manipuri (Manipur)
 
• Mohiniyattam (Kerala)
 
• Sattriya (Assam)
 
 
 
• Where as Ministry Of Culture includes Chhau also in the list and according to Ministry Of Culture's list therea are 9 classical Dance in India.

questions.question: Apart from Gujarat, Jiviti (Jivti/Jivati) Puja is performed by married women, mainly in the state/union territory of _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Jivati puja is celebrated in the states of **Gujarat and Maharashtra**.
 
• It is celebrated in the month of **Shravan(July-August)**.
 
• Puja is performed by married women mainly.
 
• Jivti is an** incarnation of Parvati**, a goddess
